newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean arrivals dip as farmers hold stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean arrivals dip as farmers hold stocks.

text.p: Soybean arrivals in the central Indian markets dipped as farmers held back stocks in the hope of getting better prices, traders said on Tuesday.
"Arrivals were around 1,000 tonnes in the markets of central India today against 15,000 tonnes per day at the same time in the previous year," said Manoharlal Jain, a soybean broker.
Soybean was quoted at 12,200-12,600 rupees per tonne compared with 9,500-9,800 rupees a year ago, traders said.
"Farmers are looking for higher prices and they were confident that they can get at least 13,000 rupees a tonne," said Prakash Vohra, another soybean trader.
Traders said capacity utilisation in the soybean processing plants was very low in the absence of adequate raw material.
Traders said activity was extremly low in the oilmeal market as both buyers and sellers were limited.
Soymeal was quoted at $300-301 per tonne fas (free alongside ship) in bulk for export against $219-220 at the same time last year.
Indian rapeseed extraction was quoted at $115-116 per tonne, against $120 a year ago.
